## Advanced

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/advanced/>

After you click on **Advanced** under **Everest Forms → Settings**, you will be taken to the Advanced Options page.

Advanced Settings provide additional controls for logging and API access, helping you manage debugging and integrations across all your forms. You can access the Advanced Settings page from **Dashboard → Everest Forms → Settings → Advanced**.

###
Enable Log

Store the form logs by enabling this option. Enabling logs will help you debug the issue if you face any. To check the logs, please go to **Everest Forms > Tools > Logs**.

##
RestApi

Use this option to enable RestAPI and generate an API key, allowing you to submit form entries programmatically (e.g., via Postman).

Look at How to Submit Entries via RestAPI (Postman Example)

## Entries Management

### Enable scheduled entry delete

Enable this option and select the amount of days to delete the stored entries.

### Admin Approval Entries
**Pro**

This option sends an approval email to the admin so that they can approve or deny the user entries. You can choose the admin email or any custom email as the receiver. You can customize the email subject and the content. Moreover, you can also set the admin entries approval or denied waiting time in days along with the option to automatically delete the entry.

## Entry Reports & Summaries

Enable this option to receive automatic email reports of your form entries. When enabled, you will get a summary of total entries, form-wise performance, and quick links to view entries directly from your email.

Look at How to Set Up Entry Reports & Email Summaries in Everest Forms

## Plugin Management

After you click on **Plugin Management** under **Everest Forms → Settings → Advanced**, you will be taken to the Plugin Management settings page.

These settings allow you to control data removal and usage tracking for Everest Forms.

### Remove Data On Uninstall

When you enable the **Uninstall Everest Forms **option, all the data of the Everest Forms will be removed from your database once you have uninstalled the Everest Forms plugin.

### Allow Usage Tracking

You can enable this option to provide us with non-sensitive information about the plugin and add-on usage.

#### What is shared?

Enabling this option will share the following information with the developers.

- admin_email – Your email

- website_url – Your site’s URL

- wp_version – WordPress version of your site

- php_version – PHP version of your site

- mysql_version – MySQL version of your site

- server_software – Software used on your server

- is_ssl – Is your site SSL or not?

- is_multisite – Is your site a multi-site platform?

- is_wp_com – Is your site hosted on wordpress.com?

- is_wp_com_vip – Is your site hosted on WordPress.com VIP?

- is_wp_cache – Is WP Cache enabled?

- multi_site_count – How many subsites are there if multi-site?

- active_theme – Name of the active theme

- active_theme_version – Version of the active theme

- locale – Language and regional settings of your website

- timezone – Time Zone Detail

- activated plugins – List of the activated plugins

- entry count: Total number of entries submitted by the users via Everest Forms

- forms count: Total number of forms created with the Everest Forms plugin

We take the privacy of our users very seriously and we only collect the data mentioned (such as PHP version, SSL or not, WordPress plugins and themes used, etc) with their explicit consent. The collected data will be used for the improvement and compatibility testing of our plugins and add-ons. This data will help us to ensure that our plugins work seamlessly with different PHP versions, different plugins, and themes. The data will not be shared with any third-party and will be kept confidential and secure. Rest assured that your data is in good hands and will only be used to enhance your experience with our products.
Also, you will receive ocassional emails notifying you about the new features or recent security updates.

## Security

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/security/>

Manage your form’s security settings to protect uploaded files, ensure data privacy, and prevent spam.

## General

### Uploaded File Protection **Pro**

Enable this option to protect uploaded files from direct public access. When enabled, users cannot access uploaded files via direct URL, improving the security of sensitive data

Look at How to Protect Uploaded Files from Direct Access in Everest Forms?

## Integration

With the Everest Forms plugin, you can enhance your form security using different spam protection methods. These include CAPTCHA-based solutions as well as modern CAPTCHA alternatives and background anti-spam services.

CAPTCHA solutions help protect your forms by verifying that submissions are made by real users. In addition, some services work silently in the background to detect and block spam without requiring any user interaction, providing a smoother user experience.

There are three types of Captcha you can add to your forms. They are:

- reCAPTCHA v2 by Google

- reCAPTCHAv3 by Google

- hCaptcha

### reCAPTCHA v2

The reCaptcha v2 requires the user to click a checkbox indicating the user is not a robot. This will either pass the user immediately (with No CAPTCHA) or challenge them to validate whether or not they are human. This is the simplest option to integrate with and only requires two lines of HTML to render the checkbox.

Look at How to integrate the Google reCaptcha v2 on Everest Forms?

### reCAPTCHA v3

reCAPTCHA v3 allows you to verify if an interaction is legitimate without any user interaction. It is a pure JavaScript API returning a score, giving you the ability to take action in the context of your site: for instance requiring additional factors of authentication, sending a post to moderation, or throttling bots that may be scraping content.

Here is How to integrate the Google reCaptcha v3 on Everest Forms?

Note: How to generate the reCaptcha Site key and Secret key?

### hCaptcha

The ‘hCaptcha‘ is a CAPTCHA service by a company called Intuition Machines Inc which provides more reliable bot detection while being simple for humans to solve.

Looking for How to integrate the hCaptcha on Everest Forms?

### Cloudflare

Cloudflare’s Captcha feature uses advanced algorithms and machine learning techniques to evaluate user behavior, analyze patterns, and determine whether a visitor is likely a human or a bot. This helps ensure that legitimate users can access the website seamlessly while blocking or challenging suspicious or malicious traffic.

Want to check out How to integrate the Cloudflare Captcha on Everest Forms?

### Cleantalk

CleanTalk is a background anti-spam service that filters spam submissions automatically without requiring any user interaction. It ensures a smooth experience for real users while effectively blocking bots.

Want to check out How to integrate the CleanTalk on Everest Forms?

## General

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/global-general-settings/>

After you click on the global settings of Everest Forms under **Everest Forms → Settings**, you will be taken to the settings page.

General Settings are basic settings that can be customized as needed and apply to all of your created forms. Here is a simple explanation of what each option is for. You can access the General Settings page from **Dashboard → Everest Forms → Settings → General**.

## Validation Messages

The Validation settings are for users to configure the message or texts that is displayed if a user enters something that is invalid or cannot be credible. This makes it easier for your users to correct mistakes if any.

### Required

This message is displayed when a user leaves a required field empty and tries to submit the form.

### Website URL

This message appears when a user enters an invalid or incorrectly formatted website URL.

### Email

This message is shown when a user enters an invalid email address or makes a mistake while typing it.

### Email Suggestion

This message provides a suggestion when the entered email seems incorrect (e.g., typo in domain), helping users correct it.

### Confirm Value

This message is displayed when two fields that are supposed to match (like password and confirm password) do not have the same value.

### Checkbox Selection Limit

This message appears when a user selects more options than the allowed limit in a checkbox field.

### Number

This message is shown when a user enters an invalid number or incorrect numeric format.

## Miscellaneous Options

### Disable User Details

You can disable storing the IP address and the User Agent on all the forms.

### Load Fonts Locally

Enable this option to load all required fonts from your own server instead of external sources, helping improve privacy and GDPR compliance.

<https://docs.everestforms.net/docs/email-settings-2/>

You can access the Email Settings from the Settings Page from **Dashboard→Everest Forms→Settings→Email**

## Template Settings

Choose from either HTML or Plain template.
